A2.text:
Elvin is a quiet accountant in Baku, but he really loves baking. Every weekend, he makes delicious apple and walnut cakes. His grandmother is his role model. She was a famous baker in Sheki, and he uses her old recipes. Elvin’s big goal is to open a small, warm cafe in Icherisheher.

“You must aim high,” his good friend Nigar always tells him. “Life is very short. You should chase your dreams!”

So, Elvin bakes fifty cakes. On Sunday morning, he takes a small folding table to a street market near the Maiden Tower. He is very happy and excited. But suddenly, dark clouds appear and it starts to rain. The narrow street is completely empty. Elvin waits for two hours in the cold. Nobody buys a single cake. He feels very sad and loses his motivation.

“I am going home,” Elvin says to Nigar on the phone. “This was a terrible idea.”

“Wait!” Nigar says. “Do not pack your table yet. I am coming.”

Ten minutes later, Nigar arrives. She is not alone. She brings a local tour guide and ten hungry tourists.

“Wow, it smells amazing!” the guide says. He buys twenty cakes.

Elvin smiles. He is ready to bake again.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: Elvin learns to bake from his grandmother
Nigar opens a new cafe in Icherisheher
Elvin changes his job to a tour guide
Elvin wants to sell cakes but the rain almost stops him
questions.why: The story is about Elvin trying to sell his cakes at the market, facing rain, and being saved by Nigar bringing customers.

questions.q: Whose recipes does Elvin use for his cakes?
questions.why: “She was a famous baker in Sheki, and he uses her old recipes.”

questions.q: Why does Elvin want to go home early?
options: The street is empty because of the rain
He has to go to work
questions.why: Because it started to rain, the street was completely empty, and nobody bought a cake.

questions.q: Nigar buys all fifty cakes from Elvin.
questions.why: Nigar brings a tour guide who buys twenty cakes, she does not buy fifty cakes herself.

questions.q: Nigar tells Elvin he should “aim high”. What does this mean?
options: To throw things up in the air
To climb a very tall building
To set ambitious goals for yourself
To stop trying and go home
questions.why: Aiming high means trying to achieve something great, like Elvin's goal to open a cafe.

questions.q: How does Elvin feel at the end of the story?
options: He is excited to continue baking
He wants to stay an accountant forever
questions.why: “Elvin smiles. He is ready to bake again.”

B1.text:
Elvin worked as an accountant in a tall office building in Baku, but his true ambition was to open a cozy bakery in Icherisheher. He spent every weekend baking traditional Sheki sweets with a modern twist. His grandmother, a master baker, was his role model.

For a long time, opening a shop was just a distant goal. Then, his friend Nigar told him to go after it. “You have enough motivation to succeed,” she said. “Start small. Rent a stall at the weekend market near the Maiden Tower.”

Elvin baked sixty honey cakes and set up his stall early on Sunday morning. He arranged the sweets perfectly and waited for customers. Unfortunately, he faced a major setback. By noon, strong winds blew in from the Caspian Sea, and heavy rain started to fall. The tourists disappeared, and the street went completely quiet.

After three hours of freezing in the damp air, Elvin’s determination began to fade. He called Nigar. “I am packing up,” he said, feeling defeated. “Nobody wants to buy anything in this terrible weather.”

“Don’t move!” Nigar ordered. “Give me fifteen minutes.”

When Nigar finally arrived, she was holding a large umbrella. Walking behind her was a tour guide named Kamran, followed by a group of freezing tourists. Nigar had found them sheltering in a nearby museum.

“I told them you had the best sweets in the city,” Nigar smiled.

The tourists crowded around the small table. The sweet smell of honey and cinnamon was exactly what they needed. Within twenty minutes, Elvin sold every single cake.

As he folded up his empty table, the rain was still falling, but Elvin didn’t care. His dream suddenly felt a lot closer.

questions.q: What is the main theme of the story?
options: Why accounting is a boring job
How bad weather ruins weekend markets
How a friend's help saves a baker's first day
Why you need a lot of money to start a business
questions.why: Elvin almost gives up due to bad weather, but his friend Nigar brings tourists to buy all his cakes.

questions.q: What kind of weather caused problems for Elvin?
questions.why: “By noon, strong winds blew in from the Caspian Sea, and heavy rain started to fall.”

questions.q: Where did Nigar find the tourists?
questions.why: “Nigar had found them sheltering in a nearby museum.”

questions.q: Elvin ate some of the cakes because he was hungry.
questions.why: The text says he sold every single cake to the tourists, but it never mentions him eating any.

questions.q: Elvin faced a major “setback”. What does this mean?
questions.why: The bad weather was a problem that stopped him from selling his cakes and making progress.

questions.q: Why didn't Elvin care that the rain was still falling at the end?
options: He was happy because he sold all his cakes
He knew Nigar would drive him home
questions.why: He sold every single cake and his dream felt closer, so the bad weather no longer bothered him.

B2.text:
By day, Elvin was a corporate accountant in a glass tower overlooking the Baku Boulevard. But by night, his kitchen turned into a flour-dusted laboratory. He baked traditional Sheki pastries, blending his grandmother’s historic recipes with modern flavours. His ultimate ambition was to open an artisanal bakery in the winding stone streets of Icherisheher.

However, for years, he did nothing but talk about it. It was his closest friend, Nigar, who finally convinced him to go after it. “You can’t just aspire to be a baker while staring at spreadsheets all day,” she told him over tea one evening. “If you want it, you have to chase your dreams.”

Taking her advice, Elvin rented a modest pop-up stall at a weekend food market near the Maiden Tower. He stayed up all night baking eighty delicate honey-and-walnut pastries, carefully packing them in elegant boxes.

He set up his display on Sunday morning, buzzing with excitement. Unfortunately, he immediately encountered a brutal setback. Shortly after midday, the notorious Baku wind picked up, bringing a sudden, freezing downpour. The cobblestone streets emptied in minutes as people rushed indoors.

Elvin stood shivering under a leaking canvas roof for three hours. His determination evaporated completely. Feeling foolish, he pulled out his phone and called Nigar.

“I’m throwing in the towel,” he muttered, staring at the unsold boxes. “It’s pouring, I’m freezing, and clearly, this was a massive mistake.”

“Don’t you dare pack up,” Nigar commanded. “Perseverance is part of the business. Just give me twenty minutes.”

When Nigar appeared through the heavy rain, she looked like a tour guide leading an expedition. In fact, she was leading an actual tour guide—a man named Kamran—along with a dozen shivering, exhausted tourists. Nigar had spotted them taking shelter in a carpet shop and promised them the best traditional sweets in Azerbaijan.

The tourists practically sprinted to Elvin’s stall. The scent of warm cinnamon and honey worked like magic. They bought every single pastry and even asked for his business card.

Packing away his empty boxes in the pouring rain, Elvin couldn't stop grinning. The corporate spreadsheets could wait; he finally had his first real customers.

questions.q: What is the core message of Elvin's story?
options: A successful business requires expensive marketing
You should never trust the weather forecast in Baku
Office jobs are better than working in food service
Achieving a dream often requires overcoming initial difficulties
questions.why: Elvin faces a setback with the weather but succeeds because his friend helps him persevere.

questions.q: How is Elvin's baking described in the story?
options: He blends his grandmother's historic recipes with modern flavours
He only bakes things he learned on the internet
He buys frozen pastries and heats them up
questions.why: “He baked traditional Sheki pastries, blending his grandmother’s historic recipes with modern flavours.”

questions.q: Why did Elvin's determination evaporate?
options: The tourists complained about the prices
He dropped all the boxes on the ground
A freezing downpour emptied the streets
questions.why: “...bringing a sudden, freezing downpour. The cobblestone streets emptied in minutes... His determination evaporated completely.”

questions.q: Nigar bought a carpet while looking for the tourists.
questions.why: The text says she spotted the tourists taking shelter in a carpet shop, but does not say she bought a carpet.

questions.q: Nigar tells Elvin that “perseverance” is part of the business. What does this mean?
options: Spending a lot of money to start
questions.why: Perseverance means not giving up even when things get tough, like standing in the freezing rain.

questions.q: What does the final sentence imply about Elvin's future?
options: He will ask for a promotion at his accounting job
He plans to become a tour guide
He is motivated to pursue his bakery dream seriously
questions.why: “The corporate spreadsheets could wait; he finally had his first real customers.” This shows he is excited to focus on his dream.

podcast.title: A dream that changed

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What did you want to be when you were a child? Guess: what did Sam dream of becoming?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is dreams and ambitions. Leyla, what did you want to be when you were a child?
[laugh] A pilot! Then a singer, then a vet. My ambition changed every year. What about you?
A footballer. I trained every day after school. I really wanted to play for Manchester United.
So what happened?
When I was sixteen, I broke my leg. It was a big setback. I couldn't play for a year, and after that I was never fast enough.
Oh no. That must have been hard.
It was. But my coach said something I still remember: "Aim high, but don't forget to enjoy the game."
That's good advice. My role model is my aunt Nigar. She always wanted to be a doctor, but she married young and had three children.
And she gave up?
Never! At thirty-eight she went back to university. She studied at night while the kids slept. Now she's a children's doctor.
Wow. That's real determination.
And perseverance. She failed one big exam twice. The third time, she passed with the best result in her group.
Amazing. Where did she find the motivation?
She told me, "Chase your dreams while you still can. I didn't want to be seventy and still wondering."
I love that. So, Leyla, what do you aspire to now?
One day I'd like to open a small café with books — a quiet place where people can read and practise English.
A SpeakLab café! I'd come every day.
And you? Do you have a goal now?
I'm running a half marathon in the spring. It's not Manchester United, but I want to go after something difficult again.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is one dream you still have — and what is your first small step?
Mine is to finish the race — without breaking my leg. See you next time!
Bye for now!

questions.q: What is the episode mainly about?
options: Childhood dreams, setbacks and not giving up
questions.why: Sam lost his football dream, Aunt Nigar became a doctor late, and both hosts have new goals.

questions.q: Why did Sam stop playing football seriously?
options: He broke his leg at sixteen
His coach told him to stop
questions.why: "When I was sixteen, I broke my leg."

questions.q: What did Aunt Nigar do at thirty-eight?
questions.why: "At thirty-eight she went back to university."

questions.q: Aunt Nigar passed her big exam the first time.
questions.why: "She failed one big exam twice."

questions.q: "Aim high" means…
options: Find a job in a tall building
questions.why: The coach wanted Sam to have big goals — and enjoy the game.

questions.q: Why is Sam running a half marathon?
options: He wants a hard goal again after football
questions.why: "I want to go after something difficult again."
